T: There's no such thing as a free dinner.
D: A lonely cable installer decides his newest customer is going to be his best friend, whether he likes it or not.
P: Bring out the chicken when Steven asks the serving wench for a fork.
S: Roast tomato bisque, drunk from the bowl
Roast tomato bisque drunk straight from the bowl, no utensils at Medieval Times.

Toss the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the olive oil and salt and roast at 220C until soft and charred at the edges. Squeeze the garlic from its skins and blend everything with the stock and sugar until smooth. Warm through, stir in the cream and season. Blitz the basil with the extra virgin oil and a pinch of salt, and swirl over the soup in mugs. Hand it over in mugs or bowls you can drink from. No spoons.
Chip asks Steven for his chicken skin.

Scrape any fat from the skin, lay it flat between 2 sheets of baking paper on a tray and weigh it down with a second tray. Bake at 200C until golden and crisp right through, then drain on paper towel. Rub the salt with the lemon zest and paprika, and warm the honey with the chilli. Break into shards, drizzle with hot honey and sprinkle with the lemon salt.
M: Tournament roast chicken with buttered corn
Herb butter roast chicken with buttered corn.

Mash 50g butter with the garlic, herbs and lemon zest and push it under and over the chicken skin. Put the halved lemon inside. Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt around the chicken in a big roasting tin. Roast at 200C, basting with the pan juices twice, until the juices run clear and the potatoes are golden. Boil the corn for 6 minutes, then roll in the rest of the butter with the paprika and salt.
W: Cinnamon apples in golden pastry. Chip gave all the knights free cable.

Cook the apples in the butter with the brown sugar, half the cinnamon and the lemon juice until soft and sticky, then cool. Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, spoon apple onto each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork. Brush with egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and the rest of the cinnamon and bake at 200C until puffed and golden. Whip the cream softly and serve with the warm turnovers.

K: A mug of ale for me and me mate
Chip orders ale for him and his mate.
Stir the honey into the hot water and let it cool. Divide the apple juice and honey syrup between 4 big mugs or tankards. Top slowly with the cold ale and squeeze in a lemon wedge.
